entities.summary:
Louis d'Amboise (1480-1511) was a French Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a pivotal role in the Council of Trent. 

As one of the most prominent clerics of his time, d'Amboise was instrumental in shaping the theological debates that led to the reform of the Catholic Church.

His contributions to the Council of Trent had far-reaching consequences, including the establishment of the Index Librorum Prohibitorum and the development of the Tridentine Mass. 

Despite his significant influence on the Church, d'Amboise's legacy is often overshadowed by that of other prominent figures from this era.

"The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing;
he makes me lie down in green pastures,
he leads me beside quiet waters,
he refreshes my soul." (Psalm 23:1-2)

Louis d'Amboise (c. 1450–1511) was a French Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a pivotal role in the High Renaissance of France. A scion of the prominent Amboise family, Louis rose through the ecclesiastical ranks to become a trusted advisor to King Louis XII.

As the Bishop of Beauvais, Louis d'Amboise implemented numerous reforms aimed at strengthening the Catholic Church's influence in France. He also contributed significantly to the establishment of the Sistine Chapel's altarpiece and advocated for the creation of an order of monks dedicated to prayer and contemplation.

D'Amboise's tenure as a cardinal predated his appointment as Bishop of Beauvais by several years, during which time he participated in three conclaves that shaped the papacy. His diplomatic acumen facilitated crucial alliances between France and other European powers, most notably with the Holy Roman Empire.

 Louis d'Amboise's legacy extended beyond his own lifetime; his efforts helped cement the French monarchy's grip on power, paving the way for future monarchs to shape the country's destiny.
